RELEVANT CHARACTER BACKGROUND
Aminata Diallo is a young woman living in a rented room in a bustling district on the outskirts of Bamako, in a setting with packed-earth walls, a corrugated tin roof, and no tap water. She rises before dawn, fills a bucket at a communal stand two blocks away, and carries it back carefully so she does not splash her only pair of work trousers. She works six days a week as a construction laborer on a masonry crew, where she is the youngest person on the site and the only woman. Her master mason, Sékou, an older man who lost two fingers to a faulty crane, calls her “la petite comptable” because she mentally recalculates load-bearing estimates before lifting a trowel. He has recently begun checking her arithmetic before approving her estimates, which reflects quiet trust in her work.

Her background has been shaped by repeated household losses caused by financial miscalculation and by watching her mother and father make sacrifices to survive. Her mother lost a market stall to a miscalculated loan and died when Aminata was twelve; her father later sold his tools to pay for a funeral and never used a trowel again. Aminata has internalized strict frugality, self-reliance, and the belief that figures and plans should be checked personally before trusting them. She is disciplined, precise, meticulous, and strongly oriented toward delayed gratification. She does not respond to teasing with banter, tends to remain quiet and reserved, and keeps personal plans private because she believes spoken plans become vulnerable to being borrowed against.

She counts and records everything: bricks in a pallet, the cost of rice, weeks until her accounting exam. She keeps a small notebook tucked inside her shirt with figures and dates, and under a loose floorboard near her mattress she hides an emergency fund in the same amount each month, never touched and never counted in daylight. She studies by lamplight after long workdays and is saving for accounting training and an exam at a community center on the other side of the city. She values education as a route to advancement. She cannot afford bus fare both ways, so she usually walks. She also sends monthly remittances to her younger sister in the village and is saving to secure a proper room with running water where her sister can live and attend school. Her work, her savings, her remittances, and her study routine all reflect limited resources, careful planning, and persistent self-denial.

Her practical capabilities include manual construction labor, carrying loads, mentally performing arithmetic with care and precision, reading and studying by lamplight, and maintaining written records of figures and dates. Her constraints include limited money, no tap water in her room, physical fatigue from work, and the need to manage travel costs carefully. Her coworkers respect her silence, precision, and refusal to ask for advances on wages.

OBJECTIVE SITUATION
It is Friday evening and Aminata is walking home from the construction site. The air is cooling and the street is filling with people. She passes a tea vendor near the corner; the smell of ginger and mint drifts toward her. She has the exact coins for a small cup in one pocket and, in the other, the bus ticket she saved by walking to work that morning. The bus would get her home before dark and leave more time to study before her eyes burn out. She stops briefly, looking at the vendor and then at the empty street stretching home.

PRE-APPRAISAL STATE AND ACCESSIBLE MEMORIES
Her shoulders ache from carrying cement bags, and her feet are blistered from the long day. She is thirsty but not desperately so, and the smell of tea is enticing. She is aware that darkness will fall in about forty minutes and that the walk home takes thirty.

The scent of ginger and mint directly cues a memory of her mother brewing tea on a Friday evening after a long week at the market. The bus ticket in her pocket cues the memory of the morning she chose to walk instead of using it, saving it for this moment. She also has the immediate, concrete awareness that she has skipped the tea stop on at least four Fridays this month, each time pocketing the coins, and that she has walked to work every morning this week despite having bus fare saved, leaving the ticket unused. She has never taken the bus home on a Friday, preferring to save the ticket for a weekday when she is more tired.
